newsitem.title: ITALY: EMU delay talk is "playing with fire" - De Silguy.
newsitem.headline: EMU delay talk is "playing with fire" - De Silguy.

text.p: Talk of delaying the launch of European economic and monetary union (EMU) is extremely risky and could scuttle the birth of a single currency, EU Commissioner Thibault de Silguy was quoted as saying.
"Whoever says that EMU will be delayed is playing with fire because in that case the Euro would risk never being born," de Silguy told Turin daily newspaper La Stampa.
Any delay in the planned launch date would require changes to the 1991 Maastricht Treaty, which charts the course towards a currency union. EMU is scheduled to take shape in 1999.

"In order to change the timetable you have to change the treaty, which is not only extremely complicated, but would be equivalent to saying that Europe does not respect its commitments," said de Silguy.
"If it does not respect the birthdate of the Euro, Europe will no longer have political credibility," said de Silguy.
De Silguy said that nobody in a position of authority in Germany supported the idea of a delayed start to EMU.
"I have seen extremely clear declarations from the Bundesbank and from the German finance ministry, according to whom there is no possibility of changing the calendar," said de Silguy.
The EU Commissioner said he welcomed signs that Italy was prepared to take supplementary deficit-cutting steps in order to keep alive its EMU hopes but he warned against use of once-off measures.
"Beware of one off measures because the (Maastricht) Treaty lays down that the budgetary restructuring should not be limited to 1997, but should be lasting," he added.
De Silguy said he was concerned that if the dollar continued to appreciate on international currency markets it would generate inflationary pressures.
"A dollar which is too strong is not a good thing," he said.
While Germany and other countries have rushed to stamp out market rumours that the German monetary authorities were about to announce a two-year delay in EMU, talk of a slippage refuses to go away.
"It may be that there are people who want to kill EMU and therefore try to obtain a delay but this would mean the death of the project," said de Silguy.
